mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to increase liquidity in the financial markets and drive up equity prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate over the past three months signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 55% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand in the housing market, which often correlates with broader economic strength and positive equity market performance, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 60-day periods following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply-side weaknesses in the economy, which can lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 45% of the 20-day periods following an INDPRO decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate is low and payroll employment is increasing, it indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with positive economic growth and higher corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a low UNRATE and rising PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is strong but inflation (CPI) is also high, it may indicate an overheating economy, leading to potential market corrections and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 50% of the 60-day periods following strong GDP growth with high CPI, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate can lead to higher borrowing costs, reduced consumer and business spending, and negative equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 50% of the 20-day periods following a FEDFUNDS increase during tightening, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real state and local government purchases indicates increased government demand, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 60-day periods following an RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
